pairs.question: Etiamne, si te in Capitolium faces ferre vellet?
pairs.answer: Numquam voluisset id quidem; sed si voluisset, paruissem.
pairs.derivation: Laelius recounts pressing Blossius, who had just claimed he would do whatever Ti. Gracchus wished ('quidquid ille vellet, sibi faciendum putaret'). Laelius's question is introduced by the framing tag 'Tum ego:' (dropped) and asks whether Blossius would obey even an order to carry torches to the Capitol. Blossius's reply has the interleaved speech tag 'inquit' (dropped); the two surviving fragments 'Numquam' and 'voluisset id quidem; sed si voluisset, paruissem' are contiguous in the utterance once the narration 'inquit' is removed, so they are joined without ellipsis. The section marker [37] is stripped. The answer ends at its full stop, before the authorial comment 'Videtis, quam nefaria vox!'
